Role Summary: 
 Global Client Payments reconciles and validates the payments Avalara makes on behalf of clients to tax authorities. Payment volume is growing across every line of business, and the team is investing in stronger reconciliation processes and AI-enabled workflows to support that growth. This role owns an established reconciliation process and the month-end close that runs alongside it. Daily reconciliations, exception resolution, and month-end close all run to fixed deadlines that partner teams and clients rely on. The role exists to raise the accuracy and timeliness of reconciliation and to convert manual reconciliation effort into repeatable, AI-supported process that makes the work faster and more reliable. 
 How This Role Elevates Avalara: 
 Reduces compliance risk by clearing exceptions and unpaid items within published turnaround targets Enhances client experience through accurate, timely reconciliation that reduces notices and penalties Improves month-end close reliability through complete, on-time delivery Prevents errors from reaching clients by catching breaks in peer reconciliations Improves decision quality by applying critical thinking across all reconciliation work Strengthens the control environment through current procedures and audit-ready evidence Increases operational scale by using AI to surface opportunities to improve reconciliation processes Raises team capability through documentation, process improvement, and AI best-practice sharing 
 Responsibilities: 
 Own daily reconciliations of bank activity against liability records, and clear exceptions within published turnaround targets Own month-end reconciliation close and deliver complete, accurate results on deadline Own creation and resolution of unpaid items, and keep aging within target Review reconciliations completed by other analysts, and catch errors before they impact clients Own presented-item and stop-payment decisions, exercising judgment within defined control requirements Own standard operating procedure (SOP) documentation, keeping it current and audit-ready Identify and implement process and AI-enabled improvements that reduce manual effort or improve accuracy Partner cross-functionally on unresolved items, and escalate with a recommendation, not just a problem Lead within the team by driving shared work to delivery and keeping peers unblocked Raise peer capability through onboarding support, knowledge sharing, and coaching. 
 AI Expectations: 
 This role is built for someone who uses AI to create real leverage in speed, accuracy, insight, and scale. 
 How you will show up in the role today 
 Spot opportunities to use AI to surface mismatches, aging patterns, and unpaid item trends faster, and work with the team to test and validate those approaches before they touch live work Build reusable prompts for recurring tasks like drafting exception narratives, summarizing unpaid item aging, and formatting variance explanations, and strengthen them through peer input before they become part of the teams toolkit Use AI to assist with SOP drafting, updates, and version comparisons, reducing the time it takes to keep documentation current after process changes Validate every AI-generated output against source data before it informs any reconciliation decision, presented-item judgment, or stop-payment action; AI assists; it does not decide 
 How this role will evolve as AI matures 
 As AI takes on more of the routine matching work, this role will shift toward owning the exception logic itself, defining the rules, thresholds, and escalation criteria that AI workflows operate within The analyst will increasingly serve as a quality control layer over AI outputs, spotting drift, validating edge cases, and flagging where AI confidence should not be trusted Process improvement will evolve from one-off efficiency gains to identifying where AI can be consistently embedded in recurring reconciliation tasks Documentation and knowledge transfer will carry more weight, as well-structured process knowledge enables more consistent execution across the team and makes AI assistance more accurate Candidates who can demonstrate this mindset, using AI confidently today while thinking clearly about where the role is heading, will stand out. 
 Bar Raiser 
 This role exists to raise the bar for the team, not just maintain current state or restore capacity. The right candidate doesn’t just do the job well; they introduce new practices, make the people around them better, and leave the process more capable than they found it. 
 What bar-raising looks like in this role 
 Structured thinking that makes complex problems legible. This person doesn’t just resolve exceptions; they diagnose why the exception occurred, whether it signals a broader pattern, and what process change would prevent recurrence. When they escalate, they bring a clear problem statement, the relevant data, and a recommended path forward. title: Supply Chain Coordinator - Level II - SHOP
description:
Job Summary The Supply Chain Coordinator - Level II is responsible for supporting material planning, inventory management, supply and demand coordination, and timely receipt and availability of materials to support business and customer requirements. The role uses planning systems, inventory data, statistical analysis, and cross-functional collaboration to maintain appropriate inventory levels, support supply and demand alignment, and drive supply chain stability. The position also manages the accurate receipt, verification, in awarding, documentation, and system entry of incoming materials while ensuring compliance with safety, quality, inventory, and material-handling procedures. Key Responsibilities Material Planning Supply Chain Coordination Analyze supply and demand requirements and identify potential risks and areas of concern over the planning horizon. Support the development and maintenance of disaggregated demand, supply, and inventory plans aligned with customer requirements. Monitor planning-system signals for abnormal demand, inventory levels, shortages, excess inventory, and other supply chain exceptions. Review and maintain planning parameters such as minimum/maximum inventory levels, reorder points, upper/lower tracking signals, and inventory segments . Perform planning parameter simulations to evaluate potential impacts on supply chain KPIs and provide detailed and executive-level reports. Make approved adjustments to planning parameters and forecast information to align detailed plans with aggregate demand requirements. Support Plan for Every Part (PFEP) activities to ensure the right part is available at the right time, in the right quantity, and at the right location. Use statistical analysis and planning tools to support inventory optimization and supply chain stability. Monitor supply chain performance and recommend actions to address gaps against expected service, inventory, and delivery targets. Material Receipt Inwarding Receive and verify incoming materials against Purchase Orders, Delivery Challans, Invoices, Packing Lists , and other applicable documentation. Check material quantity, identification, condition, and supporting documents to ensure receipt accuracy. Identify and report shortages, excess quantities, damages, quality concerns, and documentation discrepancies. Prepare and process GRR/GRN accurately in the applicable system and ensure timely system entry. Coordinate with Stockholders, Accounts, Production, Quality, Procurement, and suppliers to resolve material receipt and inwarding issues. Ensure received materials are made available to the appropriate departments within defined timelines. Maintain accurate and timely material receipt records and supporting documentation. Inventory Management Support inventory accuracy through regular stock verification and physical-to-system reconciliation. Monitor inventory levels and identify opportunities to prevent shortages, excess inventory, obsolete stock, or supply disruptions. Apply inventory management principles to optimize stock levels within defined operational and customer constraints. Ensure appropriate material segregation, identification, storage, and handling practices. Follow FIFO/FEFO requirements where applicable. Support the maintenance of accurate inventory master data and planning parameters. Analyze inventory-related KPIs and support corrective actions to improve inventory performance. Systems, Data KPI Management Use materials planning and supply chain systems as the primary tools for managing supply and demand plans, inventory, and exception messages. Use appropriate analytical tools such as Excel, Access, TOAD, OMS , or other approved applications to support analysis and problem solving. Review planning and inventory data for accuracy and take appropriate action on exceptions based on root-cause analysis. Maintain and monitor supply chain and material receipt KPIs. Analyze KPI trends and performance gaps and identify actions to improve delivery, inventory, quality, and process efficiency. Prepare reports and communicate supply chain performance, risks, and improvement opportunities to relevant stakeholders. Quality, HSE Compliance Follow established standard work, process documentation, quality procedures, and material-handling requirements. Perform quality checks on planning parameters, inventory data, material receipts, and system transactions. Comply with applicable Health, Safety Environmental (HSE) standards, policies, procedures, and regulations. Report work-related injuries, illnesses, incidents, hazards, material-handling risks, or unsafe conditions. Complete required HSE, quality, and functional training. Ensure material receipt, storage, and handling activities comply with applicable company procedures and safety requirements. Cross-Functional Collaboration Continuous Improvement Communicate effectively with Supply Chain, Procurement, Warehouse, Production, Quality, Finance, Accounts, Stockholders, suppliers, and other support functions. Coordinate with suppliers and internal teams to resolve material receipt, supply, inventory, and planning issues. Participate in quality, safety, material flow, process improvement, and supply chain optimization projects. Identify opportunities to improve material flow, inventory accuracy, planning processes, and operational efficiency. Support implementation of process improvements and standard work. Complete assigned training and personal development activities aligned with business requirements and career objectives. Remain flexible and support additional activities required to meet business and customer goals. Skills Experience Required Some relevant work experience with intermediate-level knowledge gained through education, training, or on-the-job experience. Experience in material planning, inventory management, warehouse operations, supply chain coordination, or material receipt/in warding . Understanding of purchase orders, delivery challans, invoices, packing lists, goods receipt processes, and material documentation. Experience with GRR/GRN processing and inventory/system transactions. Ability to identify material shortages, excess, damages, discrepancies, and documentation issues. Basic understanding of supply and demand planning, inventory levels, reorder points, and planning parameters. Experience with physical stock verification and physical-to-system reconciliation. Knowledge of material handling, segregation, storage, FIFO/FEFO , and inventory control practices. Ability to analyze inventory and supply chain data and identify exceptions or trends. Working knowledge of Microsoft Excel and other relevant supply chain or business applications. Strong attention to detail and accuracy in system transactions and documentation. Good communication, coordination, problem-solving, and organizational skills. Ability to work effectively with suppliers and cross-functional teams. Understanding of HSE, quality, and standard work requirements within a manufacturing or supply chain environment. 
 Preferred Experience working with ERP/MRP/material planning systems . Exposure to PFEP, supply planning, demand planning, inventory optimization, or planning parameter management. Experience monitoring and reporting supply chain KPIs. Experience in manufacturing, automotive, engineering, or industrial environment. Knowledge of tools such as Access, TOAD, OMS , or similar analytical and supply chain applications. Experience participating in continuous improvement, material flow, inventory optimization, or process improvement initiatives. Competency Technical Functional Competencies Materials Planning System Utilization: Uses materials planning systems to manage supply and demand plans, analyze exception messages, and support root-cause-based corrective actions. Plan for Every Part (PFEP): Applies PFEP principles to ensure the right material is available at the right time, quantity, and location while considering master data, planning parameters, material flow, transportation, and warehousing. Inventory Management Optimization: Uses data and analysis to determine appropriate inventory levels while balancing customer requirements, warehouse constraints, cost, and supply chain objectives. Materials KPI Management: Monitors and interprets supply chain KPIs, identifies performance gaps, and takes actions to improve delivery, inventory, quality, and customer impact. Network Master Supply Planning: Supports the alignment of supply and demand plans through analysis and cross-functional collaboration while considering service, finance, and supply chain objectives. Material Receipt Inventory Control: Ensures accurate receipt, documentation, system entry, storage, reconciliation, and control of incoming materials. Data Analysis: Uses planning and analytical tools to identify trends, exceptions, discrepancies, and opportunities for improvement. Process Quality Management: Follows established processes and identifies opportunities to improve process consistency, quality, and efficiency. 
 Behavioral Competencies Communicates Effectively: Clearly communicates supply chain requirements, risks, issues, and performance information to different stakeholders. Drives Results: Takes ownership of assigned activities and consistently delivers accurate and timely results. Global Perspective: Considers the broader supply chain and customer impact when addressing operational issues. Manages Complexity: Analyses large volumes of data and sometimes conflicting information to identify appropriate solutions. Optimizes Work Processes: Identifies opportunities to improve processes, material flow, inventory performance, and operational efficiency. Values Differences: Recognizes and respects different perspectives while collaborating with diverse teams and stakeholders. Decision Quality: Makes sound and timely decisions within established processes and approval requirements. Qualifications High school diploma or certificate of completion of secondary education, or equivalent relevant experience that meets applicable regulations. A diploma, associate degree, or bachelor s degree in supply chain management , Logistics, Operations, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related discipline is preferred. Relevant certifications in supply chain, inventory management, logistics, or materials management may be advantageous. The position may require licensing or eligibility in accordance with applicable export control or sanctions regulations.
